Application Materials.content:
For PGT courses, and some PGR courses, you'll provide a personal statement. It should share your motivation and enthusiasm for your chosen course, show your suitability for postgraduate study, include examples of relevant work, voluntary or study experiences, and incorporate skills such as time management, project management, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. You should also cover successes and achievements relevant to the course and outline why you have chosen the course, chosen Newcastle University, and how you will apply your current skills, knowledge and experience. You may also consider showing how the course fits into your career plans and ambitions.
You'll need to include contact details for **two referees**. At least one referee should be able to comment on your academic ability. Newcastle will contact referees to request references, usually at the same time as sending the conditional offer. If you already have a reference from your referee(s), you can attach it in the application portal; the reference must be signed by your referee, dated and on official letterhead. Where you have attached the reference, Newcastle may also contact your referees for confirmation.
Check the 'How to Apply' tab on your course page to see what documents to include. The main documents the University requires for postgraduate programmes are:
- a transcript of your degree studies. This is an academic record of the subjects you’ve studied and the grades/marks achieved. If you are still studying you should provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date.
- certificates to confirm your degree or highest qualification, if your degree is complete
- evidence of your English language ability
- a copy of your passport
- a curriculum vitae
- a research proposal for research programmes, if your course requires one
- a Personal Statement
- a portfolio. This is only for some creative courses; check the 'How to Apply' tab on the course page to find out if you need to include one.
- any transcripts of marks or certified documents should be translated into English
Newcastle does not need you to send any pre-university qualification documentation or any non-academic certificates of achievement.
To attach document(s) to your application, select ‘Supporting Documentation’ from the left-hand menu. There will be a list of required documents. Complete the following steps:
- Click 'Upload Documents' to find and select your document
- Select the document type from the dropdown list
- Click 'Choose files' to upload your document
- Click 'Submit'
Before you can submit your application, you must attach a copy of any mandatory documents including your degree transcript. If you are still studying you should provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date. When you upload these documents you must select the document type, such as 'transcript' or 'translated transcript'.

Interview Requirements.content: For international students or students from the EU, EEA or Switzerland who need a visa to study in the UK: “You may also be subject to academic and English language qualification verification, confirmation of funds and credibility interviews.”

Application Deadlines.content:
**Start Dates:** The course starts in **September**.
**Closing Dates:** There is no application closing date for this course, but Newcastle recommends that you apply by the **start of September**. International students are suggested to apply **at least two months before the course starts**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A 2:2 honours degree**, from a UK university, or international equivalent.
- Typically, you will have a business background and sufficient competence in statistics (eg probability theory, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, simple regressions) or a computing or mathematics/statistics background.
- For applicants from China: Students with a **4-year bachelor's degree from a recognised Chinese university** may be considered for entry onto a postgraduate course. Newcastle assesses applications using a **4 tier system**; requirements vary by course and depend on which tier the university belongs to.
- For most postgraduate courses (2026 entry), the China-specific equivalent for a **2.2** is **70%** from a Tier 1 or 2 University, or **75%** from a Tier 3 or 4 University.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- **IELTS 6.5 overall** with a minimum of **6.0 in all sub-skills**. If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- **Pearsons 70 overall** with a minimum of **65 in all sub-skills**. If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- **Duolingo 125 overall** with a minimum of **110 in Listening, 115 in Reading, 115 in Speaking, and 125 in Writing** sub-skills. If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- **TOEFL IBT or TOEFL IBT Special Home Edition prior to 21 January 2026:** **90 overall** with a minimum of **19 in Listening, 20 in Reading, 22 in Speaking, and 20 in Writing** for sub-skills. If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- **TOEFL IBT or TOEFL IBT Special Home Edition after 21 January 2026:** **4.5 overall** with a minimum of **3.5 in Reading, 3.5 in Listening, 3.5 in Speaking, and 4 in Writing** for sub-skills. If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- We often accept a wide range of English language tests and qualifications. See our English Language requirements web pages for more information. If you have a query, you can contact our International Recruitment Team.
- **PSE 6 weeks:** **IELTS 6.0 overall** with a minimum **5.5 in all sub-skills**. You can study our Pre-sessional English course at the Newcastle University International Study Centre.
- **PSE 10 weeks:** **IELTS 5.5 overall** with a minimum of **5.5 in all sub-skills**. You can study our Pre-sessional English course at the Newcastle University International Study Centre.

Program Overview.content:
Unlock the future with Newcastle University's MSc in Business Analytics. The MSc in Business Analytics gives you the skills and knowledge to thrive as a business analyst, operations analyst, consultant, or data analyst, capable of operating across a wide range of functions and industries.
Key features include:
- Comprehensive skill development: you will gain a versatile set of business analytics skills that you can apply across diverse sectors.
- Tool proficiency and critical insight: you will develop expertise in analytical tools and cultivate a critical mindset for data-driven decision-making.
- Practical project experience: you will work on real-world business analytics projects, bridging theory and practice.
- Experiential learning: you will engage with real industry challenges through hands-on learning and gain valuable exposure to current business practices.
The programme does not just teach technical skills. It also emphasises critical thinking. You will learn how to approach business analytics projects strategically and understand how to extract maximum value from data, a crucial skill in modern decision-making.
The programme is structured around three interconnected pillars:
- Semester 1 - Foundations of Data Science: you will develop core competencies in statistics and programming, specifically tailored to business analytics applications.
- Semester 2 - Managerial Perspectives: you will gain insights into the strategic and operational management of business analytics projects, focusing on effective implementation and impact.
- Semester 3 - Real-World Application: you will apply your skills in practical contexts and critically evaluate analytics solutions across different business environments.
The programme culminates in a substantial individual research project. This allows you to apply your learning to a real-world business problem and demonstrate your analytical capabilities in depth.
Our Business Analytics MSc provides you with a rigorous and comprehensive foundation in data-driven decision-making. It covers both the theoretical and practical aspects in depth. You will develop core expertise in data analytics for business insights, statistical foundations of data science, statistical learning, and research methods for business analytics. You will also acquire practical, industry-relevant skills in project management, web and social media analytics, operations analytics, artificial intelligence in business, marketing analytics, teamwork, presenting, and report writing.
You will explore how to leverage data analytics for strategic business insights. You'll apply your knowledge through a collaborative group project designed to simulate real-world challenges. By the end of the programme, you'll be able to extract actionable insights from complex datasets and make informed, data-driven decisions.
Depending on your modules, you'll be assessed through a combination of design or creative project, dissertation, essay, oral presentation, problem-solving exercises, report, reflective log, and research proposal.
Throughout your studies, you'll have access to support from academic staff, academic advisers and research supervisors, the University Student Services Team, student representatives, and peers. You'll also be assigned an academic member of staff, who will be your academic adviser throughout your time with us.
Our staff include [Nick Howey](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/nickhowey.html) (Degree Programme Director), [Dr Josephine Go Jefferies](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/josephinego-jefferies.html), [Dr James Bentham](https://search.ncl.ac.uk/s/redirect?collection=neu-meta&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncl.ac.uk%2Fmaths-physics%2Fpeople%2Fprofile%2Fjamesbentham.html&auth=p4yf1AazPqczflFNi%2FlgFg&profile=_default&rank=1&query=james+bentham), Dr Ajinkya Tanksale, [Dr Davit Marikyan](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/davitmarikyan.html), [Dr Haiyan Liu](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/haiyanlu.html), [Dr Paul Liu](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/paulliu2.html), and [Dr Aamir Khan](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/maths-physics/people/profile/aamirkhan.html).
Skills development is a central focus of the Business Analytics MSc. The programme will help you build a robust and versatile skill set valued across industries. You will enhance your ability to analyse complex business scenarios, make informed data-driven decisions, and communicate insights effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experiential learning allows you to apply advanced analytical tools and techniques to real-world problems, bridging the gap between academic theory and industry practice.
The Postgraduate Semester Abroad is an opportunity to study a complementary subject for one semester at a European partner university on an exchange basis. The experience takes place at the end of your studies, once you have submitted your dissertation/final project. Studies undertaken at a partner university will not count towards a double/dual degree award, but you'll receive a transcript from your host university evidencing your achievements. Students who complete this scheme will not be eligible for the UK graduate work visa.
Upon completing the programme, you will be well-prepared to lead data-driven innovations across various industries. The MSc in Business Analytics could lead to analytics-related roles such as business analyst, data analyst, consultant, market analyst, or quantitative analyst. These roles could cover sectors including retail enterprises, professional services firms, marketing and media-based businesses, pharmaceutical-based businesses, telecommunications companies, information technology-based organisations, consultancy firms, government and public services, and educational institutions.
Career development and employability are woven throughout teaching, learning and student experience. Business School students get access to both the wider University careers service and exclusive Business School events and resources, including one-to-one career support, industry-specific career events, online career learning tools, career planning and information sessions, an annual careers week, networking opportunities, specialist careers and business start-up support, and the chance to apply for work experience opportunities while studying.
Newcastle University Business School is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://www.aacsb.edu/), [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](https://efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), and [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](https://www.associationofmbas.com/about-us/). Only **1% of business schools worldwide** hold this triple crown. The Business School is also one of 140 business schools worldwide to be accredited by the EQUIS scheme for managerial and entrepreneurial skills development.
Newcastle University Business School is one of the largest Schools in the University, with over 4,000 students from over 85 countries. The Business School is the gateway to [Newcastle Helix](https://newcastlehelix.com/home), a landmark 24 acre hybrid city quarter that brings together researchers, business and communities. Facilities include computer clusters, lecture theatres, seminar and teaching spaces, a dedicated Student Hub and Quiet Space, study pods and bookable rooms, employability support and event hubs, a Bloomberg lab with over 20 terminals, and an Experimental and Behavioural Economics Lab.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living costs cover expenses other than tuition fees, such as accommodation, food, drink, travel and study materials. The average cost of living for a student studying in the UK is just over **£1,100 per month**.
Estimated monthly costs while studying at Newcastle:
- Rent in University-owned or managed partnership accommodation, including bills such as electricity, water, gas and wifi: **Postgraduate: £392 – £940**.
- Groceries: **£144**.
- Socialising: **£99**.
- Mobile phone: **£16** (SIM only).
- Course costs, including books, stationery, photocopying, field trips, specialist materials or equipment: around **£11 - £59 per month**.
For international students, as part of the visa application, you’ll have to prove you have sufficient funds to support yourself while at university in the UK. International students will also have further costs associated with studying in the UK, such as a student visa and a health surcharge to access the NHS.

Financial Aid.content:
**You may be eligible for a scholarship worth 25% off the international fee**. [Search our funding database](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/postgraduate/fees-funding/).
We support our EU and international students by providing a generous range of Vice-Chancellor's automatic and merit-based scholarships. See our [searchable postgraduate funding page](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/postgraduate/fees-funding/search-funding/) for more information.
If you're applying for funding, always check the funding application deadline. This deadline may be earlier than the application deadline for your course. For some funding schemes, you need to have received an offer of a place on a course before you can apply for the funding.

Multiple Applications.content: You may have received multiple programme offers, but please note that you can only accept one. Once you confirm your acceptance, all other offers—including applications still awaiting decisions—will be automatically declined. However, if you change your mind, you can request to reinstate a previously declined offer, subject to availability.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Once you've received your offer, you have three choices: accept, decline or defer.
If you decide to defer your offer, log in to the application portal you applied through to let us know. For most courses, you can defer your offer to the next academic year. If we’re able to defer your offer and you have a deposit condition outstanding, we’ll apply a January deposit condition for the following year. We’ll decline your current offer and send you a new offer for the next academic year. If we are unable to defer your offer, we’ll ask you to apply again the following year. You can only defer your offer once. To defer for a further year, you’ll need to submit a new application the following year.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
There are two types of offer you can receive: unconditional and conditional.
- You’ll receive a conditional offer if there are conditions that you need to meet before you can start your course. The conditions of your offer are in the ‘Terms and Conditions of your Offer’ section of your offer document, and can also be seen in the application portal you applied through.
- To provide evidence that you’ve met the conditions of your offer, upload your supporting documents to the application portal you applied through. If you’re still studying, upload the documents as soon as they’re available. If your supporting documents aren’t in English, you must provide certified English language translations.
- When your documents demonstrate that you’ve met your offer conditions, your offer will become unconditional. If you have just missed the conditions of your offer, Newcastle encourages you to upload your results anyway; they will review your application and may still be able to give you a place on your chosen course.
- Academic conditions include a transcript of your degree studies and your degree certificate or a certified copy.
- English language conditions can be met by taking an [international language test](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/international/language/#overview) such as IELTS, TOEFL, or Pearsons, or by completing one of Newcastle’s six- or ten-week English language courses at the [International Study Centre](https://nclisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english).
- When you’ve accepted your offer and met any conditions, Newcastle will send a Confirmation of a Place (COP) document. This is formal confirmation of acceptance of the unconditional offer.
